title: Implement JIT Privileged Access and Audit Evidence Assembly for Residency‑Bound Resources
creator: Liam O'Connor
description:
Summary:
Build a Just-In-Time (JIT) privileged access flow for residency-bound resources combined with an automated evidence assembly pipeline that produces audit-ready, signed artifacts for periodic reviews. The goal is to reduce standing privileged accounts, minimize blast radius for on-prem/VPC tenants constrained by data residency, and ship reproducible evidence bundles (access logs, SAML/SCIM reconciliations, short-lived credential issuance proof, and retention-policy snapshots) to satisfy auditors and internal compliance teams.

Context:
- Customers in regulated regions require proof that elevated access is time-limited and that any exceptions are recorded with chain-of-custody metadata.
- Current access model supports RBAC + SCIM + SSO, but privileged roles are often long-lived and proof-of-access requires manual aggregation across systems.
- This ticket ties together: time-bound SAML assertions, SCIM delta reconciliation, ephemeral role issuance (JIT), retention-aware evidence packaging, and an automated report export that can be pinned to a tenant residency and retention policy.

Non-goals:
- Replacing the full identity provider; we integrate with existing SAML/SCIM providers.
- Implementing a universal consent UX for all customers (we provide standardized flows and APIs).
acceptance_criteria: JIT access flow can issue ephemeral role tokens (TTL configurable) for residency-scoped resources via an API + console flow
Every JIT grant produces a signed, immutable record (SHA256 signature) that includes user, approver (if required), IAP, reason, start/end timestamps, and residency tag

Automated evidence assembler can produce a single audit bundle for a given date range and tenant that includes: SCIM reconciliation diffs, SAML assertion logs, JIT issuance logs, retention-policy snapshot, and a manifest with signatures
Retention settings are annotated on artifacts and the evidence assembler enforces retention policy when exporting (respecting residency boundaries)
End-to-end tests that simulate a privileged access request, approval flow, token issuance, and evidence export pass in CI with synthetic tenant data
Documentation and runbook are published and linked from the Console’s Compliance page
Security review completed and sign-off recorded in ticket comments
design_notes:
Design overview:
1) JIT issuance service sits in the private control plane and accepts OAuth-backed requests from the Console or API. For SAML flows, the IdP triggers a short-lived assertion exchange which is validated server-side.
2) Ephemeral tokens are scoped to residency tags (region/tenant) and include a cryptographic proof blob (signed by the control plane KMS) that can be stored in evidence bundles.
3) SCIM delta processor runs incremental reconciliation and stores compact diffs with timestamps; diffs reference JIT events to show who had access when.
4) Evidence assembler composes: diffs, assertion logs, token proof blobs, retention snapshots, and a manifest.json. The manifest contains canonical SHA256s for each artifact and a signed root signature.
5) Exporter supports two outputs: a zip (for human review) and an OCI image-style artifact (for long-term machine-consumable archiving).

Trade-offs considered:
- We considered storing full assertion payloads (large) vs. canonicalized digests — we chose digests plus essential fields to balance auditability and residency/retention constraints.
- Approval workflows: immediate auto-approve for low-risk ops vs. manual approval for sensitive roles. We will ship auto-approve for scoped developer access first and require manual approval for privileged ops.

Security/Privacy:
- All exported bundles are encrypted with tenant KMS when residency mandates it.
- Signatures use HSM-backed keys where tenant KMS not available.
- Access to assembler is audited and rate-limited.
tasks: API: create JIT token request/response schema and endpoints (ENG)
Console: add JIT request UX and approver flows (DES + PM)
Service: implement ephemeral token generation + KMS/HSM signing
SCIM: extend reconciliation service to emit compact deltas with JIT correlation IDs
Assembler: implement bundling, manifest generation, and export formats
E2E: write CI tests to simulate tenant residency and retention enforcement
Docs: compliance runbook, reviewer checklist, and Console help text
Security: schedule review and integrate findings
progress_updates: 2026-02-26 - Kickoff: scoped requirements with PM (Sofia Martinez) and security (Ravi Desai). Decided to prioritize developer/ops JIT and postpone privileged ops UX until phase 2.

2026-03-03 - Prototype: generated proof blob format (JSON-LD + SHA256) and validated KMS signing flow in dev environment. Shortcoming: KMS cross-region latency — plan to cache signatures for 30s for UX responsiveness.
2026-03-10 - Integration: SCIM delta emitter implemented in branch feat/scim-delta-assembler. Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4827
2026-03-12 - Blocker addressed: Console team provided mockups for approval flow; awaiting final accessibility review from Design.
